question: Which statement best describes [param] — a single dynamic segment?
options: A page (and layout) for a dynamic segment receives a `params` object whose keys are the segment names. In Next 14 you read it synchronously; in newer versions `params` is a Promise you `await`. Use it to fetch the matching record. Layouts and other special files at the same depth get the same `params`.

Doubling the brackets makes the catch-all optional: `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` matches the parent `/shop` (with `params.slug === undefined`) AND `/shop/a/b`. Use it when one page should handle both the index and nested paths — e.g. a category page that also renders the storefront root.

Naming a folder `[id]` turns that URL segment into a parameter. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` matches `/blog/hello` and `/blog/world`, and the captured value arrives in the page's `params` prop as `{ slug: 'hello' }`. One file serves an unbounded set of similar pages — the classic blog/product/user-profile pattern.

A folder named `[...slug]` matches one OR MORE path segments and collects them into an array. `app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx` matches `/docs/a`, `/docs/a/b`, `/docs/a/b/c` and gives `params.slug = ['a','b','c']`. Great for arbitrarily-deep docs trees or file-path-like URLs. Note: it does NOT match the bare `/docs` parent.
explanation: Naming a folder `[id]` turns that URL segment into a parameter. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` matches `/blog/hello` and `/blog/world`, and the captured value arrives in the page's `params` prop as `{ slug: 'hello' }`. One file serves an unbounded set of similar pages — the classic blog/product/user-profile pattern.

question: Which statement best describes Accessing params in a page?
options: Export an async `generateStaticParams` from a dynamic page to tell Next which param values to pre-render at build time, turning the route into SSG. It returns an array of params objects (e.g. `[{ slug: 'hello' }]`). Combine with ISR (`revalidate`) to refresh them, and control whether unknown params render on-demand or 404 via `dynamicParams`.

question: Which statement best describes [[...slug]] — optional catch-all?
options: `params` are path segments defined by your folder names (`/blog/[slug]`); `searchParams` are the query string (`?page=2&sort=asc`). A page receives both as props. Crucially, reading `searchParams` makes the route dynamic (rendered per request), while `params` alone can stay static via generateStaticParams.

Type the props so params keys match your folder names: a `[slug]` page uses `{ params: { slug: string } }`, and a catch-all uses `{ params: { slug: string[] } }`. In Next 15+ these become Promises (`Promise<{ slug: string }>`) that you await. Typing catches mismatched param names early.
